determinism.note: Original native CUDA scatter reductions may differ by float32 rounding. Numerical equivalence uses the declared tolerances; bitwise repeatability is not claimed. Strict deterministic-algorithm mode is not forced because unsupported native scatter would test a different execution restriction.

model_source.neighbor_backend: installed torch.cdist/topk KNN; no radius-Warp execution

gradient_check.definition: gradient(mean_B mean_NTC MSE) versus sum_B gradient(B1 MSE)/B, same eval weights

budget_note: Timing compares equal 2-simulation workloads: B separate original B1 calls versus one native batch. Forward-backward timing uses one accumulated mean gradient and no optimizer update in either path. The separate Adam probe performs exactly 3 updates and 6 simulation observations. B1's 3 updates observe 3 simulations; matching epochs with batch B reduces updates to ceil(train_count/B). Timing benefit alone does not establish equal training convergence or equal optimizer-update budgets.
timing_note: One correctness forward and one correctness backward warm each path before two default timed repetitions. CUDA synchronization brackets each timing. Inputs/labels already reside on GPU; adapter layout/graph preparation is included, disk reading and transfer excluded. Allocator peaks cover phase work and live tensors, not driver VRAM. Both forward paths retain all B simulation outputs until after synchronization/memory sampling. RSS is a phase-boundary snapshot; windows_process_peak_wset_bytes is process-wide context, not a per-phase CPU peak. No test labels or held-out cases are opened.
